svg.title: QP2609 Q4 - D7: blending on board (SEA-Mate BOB) - conceptual functional diagram
svg.desc: A third-party oil-preparation unit, not an Everllence or WinGD system and not the lubricator. A: the blending components - the in-use system oil (from the main-engine sump, cleaned by the purifier and held in a system-oil settling tank; fresh system oil tops up the sump) and two bunkered cylinder-oil products, a high-BN product in tank 1 and a low-BN product in tank 2. B: the blending-on-board unit, a skid with PLC control, blends system oil and/or the low-BN oil with the high-BN product to a set BN; the operator enters the fuel sulphur, and some models accept a signal input. C: the blend fills a day tank of "fit-for-purpose" cylinder oil. The supplier also draws the ship's product line continuing to the day tank; its use is not described. D: from the day tank the oil takes the engine's existing supply path to the lubricators, which - not the blending unit - meter the oil, set the feed rate and inject it into the liner. The unit's internal pumps, meters, mixer, heating and filtration are not published and are not drawn. No BN values, blend ratios or capacities are given.
svg.text: Q4 - D7 BLENDING ON BOARD (BOB) - prepares cylinder oil; it is NOT the lubricator
Conceptual functional diagram after the supplier's published set-up diagram (SEA-Mate Blending-on-Board, Marine Fluid Technology).
Not Maersk's or any ship's piping. A separately installed unit - not an Everllence or WinGD system, and not required by any engine type.
CONCEPTUAL: the unit's internals (pumps, meters, mixer, heating, filtration) are not published and not drawn. No BN values or ratios.

Not the same as ACOS2 or ACOM Mk III
ACOS2 (D3): switches between two finished cylinder oils
ACOM Mk III (D4): the engine maker's option that mixes two
finished cylinder oils on the supply line to an ordered BN
BOB: a separately installed unit that blends a base stream
with a high-BN product and fills a day tank
none of the three meters oil into the cylinder
Checking the blend and the engine
the blend tolerance is a supplier figure, not independently shown
drain-oil (scrape-down) analysis continues as the engine
designer specifies: on-board test kit and laboratory
WinGD applies its residual-BN / iron charts to oils blended on board
Not established by the sources: an Everllence service letter on BOB; engine-maker approval of a given blend; use in gas mode on dual-fuel engines.
Sources: Marine Fluid Technology - SEA-Mate Blending-on-Board brochure (11/2019) p.2 set-up diagram; BOB two-pager (08/2018); case studies Clara Maersk (2016)
and JS Greensail - Evergas (02/2021); WinGD Lubricants guideline DTAA001621 rev B (25 Nov 2025). Original MIW drawing: the supplier's artwork is not reproduced.
